name: Charikot
blurb: The district headquarters of Dolakha, on a ridge with a wide view of Gaurishankar and the Rolwaling peaks. It is the last town with banks and a hospital before the road drops to the Tamakoshi and turns north.
tip: Draw cash here; there is nothing reliable further up the valley.

name: Dolakha Bazaar
blurb: An old Newar trading town a few kilometres beyond Charikot, known for the open-roofed shrine of Dolakha Bhimsen. The road to Singati and the Rolwaling trailhead passes through on its way down to the Tamakoshi.

name: Kalinchok
blurb: A hilltop shrine to Kalinchok Bhagwati above the lodge village of Kuri, north of Charikot. A cable car and a stone staircase lead to the top, which draws Nepali visitors for winter snow and a long mountain skyline.

name: Singati
blurb: A hot riverside bazaar on the Tamakoshi where most public buses from Charikot terminate. Shared jeeps continue up the hydropower road through Jagat and Gongar to Chetchet.

name: Chetchet
blurb: A few shops and very simple lodges on the Tamakoshi road beside a tall waterfall. The Rolwaling trail leaves the road here, crosses the river on a suspension bridge and climbs straight up to Simigaon.

name: Simigaon
blurb: A terraced Sherpa and Tamang village on a spur high above the Tamakoshi, with a monastery at its top end and a first view of Gaurishankar. The climb from the road is about 600 m of stone steps.

name: Dongang
blurb: Two or three simple lodges in a forest clearing beside the Rolwaling Khola, the only practical overnight stop between Simigaon and Beding. Expect shared rooms and dal bhat.

name: Beding
blurb: The main village of the Rolwaling Sherpas: stone houses, a monastery and a school beside the river, with the south side of Gaurishankar directly above. Many Everest climbing Sherpas come from here.
tip: Spend two nights here; the jump from Dongang is close to 900 m.

name: Na
blurb: The summer settlement of the Rolwaling Sherpas on a broad valley floor, lived in from about May to October. A few lodges open in the trekking seasons and serve as the base for Tsho Rolpa and the Yalung valley.
tip: Ask in Beding whether the lodges here are open; outside the main seasons the settlement can be empty.

name: Tsho Rolpa
blurb: A grey-green glacial lake about three and a half kilometres long, held back by a moraine at the snout of the Trakarding Glacier. It is one of the largest glacial lakes in Nepal and among the most closely monitored.
tip: Keep to the path on the moraine crest; the inner slopes above the water are loose and undercut.

name: Tashi Lapcha
blurb: The glaciated pass at the head of the Rolwaling valley that leads over to Thame in Khumbu. It involves glacier travel, slopes exposed to rockfall and at least two high camps, and is a mountaineering route, not a trek.

name: Deurali
blurb: A hamlet with a few small hotels in a saddle on the Kalinchowk road, at about 2,330 m and an hour or so on foot from Charikot. The long climb to Kuri begins here, with next to no shelter on the way up.

name: Kuri
blurb: The lodge village below the Kalinchowk shrine, at the end of the rough road from Charikot and beside the lower station of the cable car. Its height is published as anything from 3,200 to 3,450 m; the ground itself is at about 3,370 m.
tip: Rooms are unheated, and it freezes on most nights from November to March. Ask for extra quilts as soon as you arrive.
